chunks: Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'I used to spread out the bed for my father, waiting for him until he would come. So when he would lie down upon his bed and sleep, I would arise to go to my own bed. One night he was delayed, so I went to the Masjid seeking him, and that was after the people had dispersed.'
So there he was in the Masjid, prostrating, and there was no one in the Masjid apart from him, and I heard his yearning and he was saying:

'O Allah! You are my Lord, truly, truly. I am prostrating to You, O Lord, as a servant and a slave. O Allah! My deeds are weak, so Increase these for me. O Allah! Save me from Your Punishment on the Day You will be Resurrecting Your servants, and Turn towards me for You are the Oft-Turning, Merciful'.

key_terms.تَعَبُّداً وَ رِقّاً: as a servant and a slave

ai.seo_question: What was the Imam's personal supplication during night prostration?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the profound humility of Imam al-Baqir (AS) by depicting him in solitary night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl), emphasizing the Shia emphasis on personal devotion and the spiritual status of the Imams. The supplication recited, 'Subhanka Allahumma anta Rabbi haqqan haqqan,' reflects the theological concept of *Taqabbul* (acceptance of deeds) despite human weakness, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding the efficacy of the Imams' worship. It serves as a practical model for believers to emulate the Imams' intense reliance on Allah's mercy during the quiet hours of the night.
